decision.summary: No confirmed temporary offsets. Two candidate intervals are identified: (1) a prolonged unidirectional E/U descent (500–683) lacking reversal; (2) a sharp multi-axis jump at 684–690 with no return observed within allowed context. Both lack opposing returns and thus remain uncertain. N-component stability throughout supports absence of transient recovery.

intervals.observation: E-component shows sustained monotonic descent from ~−2.5 to ~−13 MAD between indices 500–660, continuing gradually to ~−14.5 by index 683; U-component declines steadily over same interval with superposed fluctuations; N remains stable. No opposing return observed within allowed context (up to 699), and the trend persists through 683 without reversal—thus not a temporary offset.

At index 684: sharp multi-axis displacement—E drops ~−11 MAD, U jumps +6.8 MAD, N rises +26.2 MAD—followed by immediate stabilization into a new plateau by index 690. Return to pre-event levels is absent; motion appears permanent or long-lasting. No opposing return observed before index 699, so status uncertain despite clear onset and interior stability.
